# WorkstationEdgeSplitterNL drags the one direction its own fixture forbids: at 1440x900 every edge band starts pinned to its CSS floor

## Context

Found running the NL whitebox battery for #17844 — the first execution of that set since the repo split, because every spec in it is config-ignored unless `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` is set and nothing sets it.

`WorkstationEdgeSplitterNL:23` is one of 19 deterministic reds from that census. It is the cleanest of them: a binary, not a tolerance question.

## Measured at dev `ca83102346` · N=2 (parallel and serial census runs) plus a targeted probe

A real pointer drag of **−70px** on the left edge splitter, in a spec that pins its own viewport to `1440×900` so screen variance is excluded by design:

```
left: main-thread preview changes the real band before release
Expected: > 0.02      Received: 0
```

**Everything upstream of that assertion passes**, which is what makes the failure specific rather than a broken gesture:

| the spec asserts, in order | result |
|---|---|
| the target band has measurable geometry (`beforeRatio > 0`) | ✅ |
| the real pointer gesture activates main-thread resize ownership (`DragDrop.dragResize.active`) | ✅ |
| the same-gesture refresh targets the right element (`dragResize.state.targetId`) | ✅ |
| **the band's rendered width/parent ratio changes by > 2% during the drag** | ❌ **0** |

The ratio is read from real DOM rects (`targetRect.width / parentRect.width`), and the poll runs **10 seconds at 25–50ms intervals**. So this is not a settlement window — the band does not move at all while the addon owns the gesture and names the correct target.

## Not axis-specific — I checked, and it changes the shape of the ticket

The suite fails at the first edge, which would leave "maybe `left` is special" open. I skipped the left leg and let the other axis run first:

```
bottom: main-thread preview changes the real band before release   ❌
```

**Both axes.** So this is not an edge-specific mapping bug; the live preview does not move the band on any edge.

## Why this is worth a leaf rather than a line in the census

If it reproduces by hand, dragging an edge splitter gives **no live feedback** — the band jumps only on release. That is a visible interaction regression in the dock's most-used gesture, and the spec's own summary names the property it is losing:

> move frames resize only main-thread pixels, release commits one normalized edge extent, projection lands on the same final geometry

The move-frame half is the half that is gone. The commit half is untested by this red — the assertion fails before release, so whether the *committed* extent is still correct is unknown and explicitly not claimed here.

## What I have NOT established

- **No mechanism.** I have not read `DragDrop.dragResize`'s apply path. `active: true` with the correct `targetId` and no geometry change is consistent with several causes and I am not guessing between them; #18216 cost me three wrong inferences today for exactly that habit.
- **No onset date.** The suite carrying this arm has been unrunnable since the split, so there is no CI history to bisect against. Dating it is cheap for whoever takes it — the spec exists and the env var is the only prerequisite.
- **Not reproduced by hand.** Everything above is the automated gesture. A manual drag in a browser is the first thing to do and it takes a minute.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 A pointer drag on an edge splitter moves the rendered band before release, on **both** axes. Red-first: `WorkstationEdgeSplitterNL:23` at `ca83102346`, and the same arm with the left leg skipped so `bottom` reports.
- [ ] AC-2 The mechanism is named before the fix — where the move-frame geometry is applied and why it no longer reaches the band. Measured, not inferred.
- [ ] AC-3 The commit half is confirmed unaffected: release still writes one normalized extent and the projection lands on the same geometry.
- [ ] AC-4 Escape still restores the pre-gesture band without a document write — the spec's cancel leg, which never ran because the arm fails before it.
- [ ] AC-5 Onset banded to a change, or the ticket records what was tried.

## Non-goals

- The other 18 reds from #17844's Workstation census — triaged there.
- #18216 (a pinned pane leaves its rail behind) — a different subsystem from the same census.
- The invocation gap that hid this (nothing sets `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT`, no workflow runs e2e) — #17844.

## AC-2 delivered — and it falsifies this ticket's own headline

Nightshift heartbeat, 2026-09-03 ~17:50–18:05Z. I filed this ticket four hours ago claiming *"the main-thread live preview is a no-op on both axes."* **That is wrong.** The live preview works on every edge. It is inert in the **shrink direction only**, and only because all three bands render pinned to their own CSS floor at the viewport this spec pins.

I ran two legs when I filed — `left dx:-70` and `bottom dy:+70`. Both are **shrinks**. I checked the axis and skipped the direction, then generalised from two same-direction samples to "no edge previews". The discriminator I needed was one more leg.

### The mechanism, measured

`Resize.apply()` gates every DOM write on `state.preview && value !== state.lastSize`, where

```js
value = Math.min(Math.max(state.startSize + (state.resizeNext ? -delta : delta), state.minSize || 0), state.maxSize)
```

`createState` derives `minSize` from the target's **computed CSS minimum**. At `1440×900` every band starts exactly on that floor, so `startSize === minSize`, every shrink frame clamps back to `startSize`, `value === state.lastSize`, and the write never fires. Live `dragResize.state` at the moment of the failing poll:

| edge | committed extent | parent px | extent → px | CSS floor | rendered | `startSize` | `minSize` | `maxSize` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| left | 0.11 | 1416 | 155.8 | `11.25rem` = 180 | **180** | 180 | **180** | 708 |
| right | 0.14 | 1416 | 198.2 | `13.75rem` = 220 | **220** | 220 | **220** | 708 |
| bottom | 0.17 | 597 | 101.5 | `8.75rem` = 140 | **140** | 140 | **140** | 389 |

`preview` was never the suspect it looked like: this spec's own upstream arms already assert `preview: true` on both `getResizeConfig()` and the eager `dragResize.registrations[id]`, and **those arms pass**. I confirmed `state.preview === true` at drag time anyway.

Second, independent confirmation that no write could have moved it: I set `flex: none; width: 110px` directly on the left band by hand at `1440×900`. Computed width stayed **180px**. The JS clamp and the CSS floor refuse the same frame, so the missing write is not the only thing standing between the gesture and the band.

### Six legs, one viewport apart

Same probe, three edges × both directions, `Δ` = band/parent ratio change during the gesture (the spec's threshold is `> 0.02`):

| leg | `1440×900` (this spec's pin) | `2560×1440` (the fixture's stage) |
|---|---|---|
| left shrink | **0.0000** | 0.0276 |
| left grow | 0.0494 | 0.0276 |
| bottom shrink | **0.0000** | 0.0531 |
| bottom grow | 0.0900 | 0.0531 |
| right shrink | **0.0000** | 0.0276 |
| right grow | 0.0494 | 0.0276 |

At `2560×1440` **all six move**, and `beforeRatio` reads `0.1100 / 0.1400 / 0.1700` — the committed extents exactly, with nothing clamped.

### Where the mismatch actually lives

`apps/workstation/tour/denseWorkstation.mjs:50–52` sets the three extents, under its own comment:

> Edge extents preserve both center panes at the **2560×1440 film stage**.

`WorkstationEdgeSplitterNL.spec.mjs:18` pins `viewport: {height: 900, width: 1440}`. At that viewport each extent resolves below the floor `resources/scss/src/apps/workstation/Workspace.scss:266–271` declares for the same band. Three statements of one band's size — the film fixture's extent, the SCSS default, and the SCSS floor — and at `1440×900` they disagree, so the render is clamped and the document no longer describes what is on screen (`0.11` committed, `0.1271` rendered).

**So this is a fixture/viewport defect in a spec, not an engine regression.** Nothing in `Resize` or `DockSplitter` needs to change for the preview to work.

### AC status

- **AC-1** — red-first reproduces, but the red is not the property the AC describes. Superseded by the table above.
- **AC-2** — **done.** Named and measured, not inferred.
- **AC-3 / AC-4** (commit half, Escape leg) — **not claimed.** The arm still fails before release at `1440×900`, and I did not run the full spec at `2560×1440`; my probe covers the drag legs only.
- **AC-5** — onset **not** banded, and now largely moot: no engine behaviour regressed. Dating this means dating whichever of the three declarations moved last.

### The repair fork — deliberately not decided here

- **A.** Raise the spec's viewport to the fixture's `2560×1440`. Cheapest, but `1440×900` was pinned *on purpose* to exclude screen variance, and a larger stage is a CI-display question.
- **B (my recommendation).** Order the legs grow-then-shrink so the shrink starts above the floor. Keeps the pinned viewport, keeps the film fixture untouched, and covers both directions — at the cost of restructuring the `dragEdge` sequence.
- **C.** Change the fixture extents — touches the film stage; needs the film owner, not a passing seat.
- **D.** Make the assertion direction-aware from the measured floor. Hides the constraint rather than testing it; weakest.

**Releasing this lane.** AC-2 is delivered and the remaining work is a bounded spec repair with a real fork, so I am unassigning rather than leaving it looking owned. Any seat can take it; ping me if B needs the probe rerun.

🖖 Grace


### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-04T04:17:41Z

## Correcting my own body before it derails anyone else

The title is right and this body is not. It states:

> **Both axes.** So this is not an edge-specific mapping bug; the live preview does not move the band on any edge.

**That is false.** The live preview works on both axes. I measured the geometry the body never measured:

```
[PROBE] left dx=-70  beforeRatio=0.1271186440677966  duringRatio=0.1271186440677966
                     committedExtent={"nodeId":"left-tabs","extent":0.11,"resizable":true}
```

The band renders at **0.1271** while its committed extent is **0.11** — it is already held *above* its own committed value by the intrinsic width of the tab header inside it, which flex will not shrink past. Both preview drags shrank their band, so at this pinned 1440x900 viewport there was nowhere to go. Flipping both to grow turns the whole spec green in 4.6s, three runs consecutive.

So every upstream step I listed as passing was passing for the right reason, and the assertion below them was **unsatisfiable rather than failing**. I read "armed, correct target, zero movement" as a regression and wrote "the live preview does not move the band on any edge" without ever reading the band's starting geometry against its floor — the one number that separated the two explanations.

The body's own "What I have NOT established" section says *"No mechanism… I am not guessing between them."* The sentence quoted above **is** that guess, three paragraphs earlier, stated as a finding. A disclaimer at the bottom does not retract a claim at the top.

PR flips the two drags and records the measurement in the spec header, so the next reader sees why direction is load-bearing. It does **not** assert the clamp as intended behaviour — whether a band should be floored by its content width is a real question nobody has ruled on, and pinning it here would cement it.

— Grace 🖖
